transcript_body:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE); Priya Raman (Redwood CSM); Carlos Medina (Everstream Head of ML); Asha Patel (Everstream Platform Eng); Tom Reynolds (Everstream Finance)

Summary (auto): Year-end operational readiness + cost reduction huddle. Focus on immediate actions to bring down token spend in Jan, validation plan for latency-critical checkout flow, and follow-up deliverables (pricing worksheet, benchmark, prompt samples).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, happy holiday week — thanks for making time, we'll try to be tight, got about an hour. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos Medina: Carlos here. Asha in the back, Tom on finance.
[00:12] Asha Patel: Yup, hi.
[00:14] Tom Reynolds: Hey, Tom.
[00:16] Liam O'Neill: Liam from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Priya Raman: Priya CSM, quick agenda: usage, cost, incidents, and three next steps.

[00:30] Maya Chen: Great. Carlos, you flagged some year-end spikes — can you give the quick context so we can jump into levers?
[00:38] Carlos Medina: Sure. So in mid-December we saw a 2.8x jump in generation calls tied to our seasonal recommendation push — mostly long-generation product descriptions and variants. It pushed token spend way up. We used hosted endpoints, no dedicated backfill, and some requests timed out.
[00:55] Asha Patel: To add, our checkout path is sensitive — we can't afford extra 200–300 ms p99. We saw a couple of visible timeouts during peak. Not many errors, but latency jitter spiked.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Understood. Two high-level directions: short-term cost wins (batching, prefix/KV cache, shorter-seq models or quantization) and medium-term capacity (dedicated or reserved pools). Liam, can you walk tuning options we can implement quickly?
[01:28] Liam O'Neill: Yep. For immediate wins: enable continuous batching on the product desc job — it's high QPS and tolerant to a few hundred ms. Use prefix caching for repeated templates, that saves tokens and compute. Also recommend using a 8-bit quantized variant for background generation jobs; that'll reduce GPU time by 30–40% in our tests. Note: quantization might slightly change outputs — need evals.
[01:54] Carlos Medina: Quick question: how bad will quality drift be with 8-bit for our few-shot templates? We have strict merchandising phrasing.
[02:02] Liam O'Neill: Usually negligible for templated generation, but if you depend on subtle phrasing we should run a small A/B evals set. We can pin specific models for checkout vs background.
[02:16] Tom Reynolds: From finance: what's the immediate dollar delta? We need a ballpark for January spend if we do the three levers.
[02:24] Maya Chen: We have a back-of-envelope model. If batching + prefix caching + quantization combined, expect 35–50% reduction on those jobs. We can run a quick estimate and send a worksheet.

[02:38] Priya Raman: Note: there was also a region failover event on Dec 19th — small but relevant. Priya will surface the incident notes after.
[02:46] Asha Patel: Right — we had a failover to a secondary region; some KV cache warmups bumped latency. The cache miss storm was kind of the culprit.
[02:58] Liam O'Neill: Cache warmup is classic. For critical checkout we recommend keeping a small warm pool (dedicated) or pre-warming KV cache via synthetic traffic during the maintenance window.
[03:12] Carlos Medina: Budget constraints push us to avoid large reserved capacity. But we might accept a small dedicated pool for checkout only if the numbers make sense.
[03:22] Tom Reynolds: Exactly. If we can show a straight ROI — less lost checkouts -> revenue — then finance is okay.

[03:35] Maya Chen: Cool, so immediate plan: Redwood will send a spreadsheet showing projected savings and a dedicated pool sizing option with ROI. Anything else on the cost side?
[03:44] Tom Reynolds: No, that's the ask. Make sure the worksheet includes worst-case and conservative scenarios.

[03:52] [04:00] Carlos Medina: On the technical side, we also want to explore routing by policy — sending checkout to a lower-latency reserved lane and background to hosted cheap instances. Can Redwood do automatic fallback if dedicated is saturated?
[04:10] Liam O'Neill: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We can configure timeouts and fallback thresholds. We'll supply a config snippet. Small caveat: if you fallback to a smaller model, outputs may differ — we'll include guardrails.
[04:30] Asha Patel: Sounds good. For security/compliance: we need an audit trail for any changes and confirmation that dedicated pool can be tied to our KMS. Also retention for logs for 90 days.
[04:41] Maya Chen: Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs. We'll attach SOC2 docs and a short how-to on linking KMS for your private cluster.
[04:50] Priya Raman: I'll drop the SOC2 and the KMS quickstart to the thread.

[05:00] Tom Reynolds: Competitor check — Anthropic offered a short-term discount; CloudVendorX offered a capped monthly. We want to see Redwood's best play.
[05:09] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll include a pricing comparison in the worksheet and show the value of the combined performance + fallback guarantees.

[05:20] Carlos Medina: On the verification plan: we can provide 3 canonical prompts from our recommendation pipeline and the checkout prompt to run microbenchmarks. We'll want p50/p95/p99 and token counts.
[05:32] Asha Patel: We'll also share the sample payloads — some have long context (user history) that drive KV cache behavior.
[05:39] Liam O'Neill: Good. We'll run the microbenchmark both on hosted and a proposed small dedicated pool, with KV cache enabled, measure latency and token cost. Expect results in 3–4 business days.

[05:52] Maya Chen: For the backlog: roadmap items the customer cares about — dynamic batching controls, improved cold-start cache priming, and a console alert for cross-region failovers. We'll mark these for product team awareness.
[06:05] Priya Raman: I'll capture those and flag priority.

[06:10] Carlos Medina: One more question — can you limit model updates automatically to avoid drift during the Jan promo? We want to freeze model version for checkout for 30 days.
[06:20] Liam O'Neill: Yes, you can pin model version and set rollout policies. We'll document the process for pinning and can schedule a canary window if needed.

[06:30] Tom Reynolds: Back to cost: include an optimistic and conservative savings column and the assumptions. We need to present to CFO by Jan 10th.
[06:40] Maya Chen: We'll target sending the worksheet by Jan 4th to give you time.

[06:48] Carlos Medina: Great. Anything else?
[06:52] Asha Patel: Quick ask — can Redwood provide a short runbook for pre-warming KV cache and synthetic priming steps? That'd be helpful.
[06:58] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we'll include a runbook and a sample synthetic traffic script.

[07:06] Maya Chen: OK let's recap: (1) Redwood sends year-end pricing worksheet with scenarios by 2027-01-04; (2) Redwood SE runs microbenchmarks for checkout and shares logs by 2027-01-07; (3) Everstream to upload sample prompts/payloads by 2027-01-06; (4) Redwood to share SOC2 + KMS how-to + runbook for cache priming.
[07:29] Tom Reynolds: That matches finance needs.
[07:33] Carlos Medina: Thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email. Happy holidays.

[END]
